Summary
: This is a study of the Brihadaranyaka-Upanishad: a major text belong to an important classification of Vedic literature. The thesis defines the Upanisads mainly as “brahmavidya” or “secret knowledge received from a teacher that destroys ignorance (avidya) and leads to Brahman/moksha”. It reviews the place of Upanishads within Vedic literature (Samhita–Brahmana–Aranyaka–Upanishad), notes debates on the number, date, and chronology of Upanishads, and highlights the ten principal Upanishads (traditionally linked to Shankara’s commentaries). The Brhadaranyaka-Upanisad is seen as the largest and among the most profound texts.
